subject: Close timeline: stagger + stitch plan and escalation
messages:
From: Eli Thompson <eli.thompson@halcyonhealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close timeline concern — staging slippage

Markus,

Thanks for checking in. Quick recap from our side: we hit a hard stop on the internal evaluation last week when our security team requested additional logs and the procurement group paused any spend until a tail-risk review completes. The effect is that our targeted go/no-go eval window (the two-week canary) is delayed by at least 2–3 weeks unless we can reopen a parallel path.

Can you send a concise risk log and a proposed MAP update we can share with our security and procurement teams? Procurement has asked for a clear list of open items and any temporary mitigations you can offer (e.g., dedicated tenancy for the canary, retention guarantees). They also want to see a short timeline showing the earliest achievable go-live with mitigations applied.

We have a procurement touchpoint on Friday; if you can get something in before then that would be ideal.

Attaching what we forwarded from security (evaluation_impact.pdf).

—Eli
Eli Thompson
Director, Platform Engineering
Halcyon Health

Attachments: evaluation_impact.pdf (summary)

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Eli Thompson <eli.thompson@halcyonhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-02T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close timeline concern — staging slippage

Eli — thanks for the note and the file. We hear you. I pulled together a short "stagger + stitch" proposal that gives you an operationally-safe path to keep the eval progressing while we address procurement/security asks. High level:

- Staggered canary: split the two-week canary into an initial 72-hour functional pass on a dedicated pool, then a second 10-day operational pass with restricted telemetry.
- Stitch controls: temporary tighter retention (30 days) + explicit KV cache isolation for your tenant during the canary.
- Evidence pack: we will produce a 1-page risk log (open items + mitigations) and an acceptance checklist for your security team.
- Procurement-friendly timeline: earliest achievable re-start = 2025-10-09 (if mitigations accepted by 10/04); go-live window shifts to 2025-11-03 — we can tighten if procurement expedites.

Next steps (asks):
1) Eli — confirm the procurement contact (procurement@halcyonhealth.com copied?) and whether a Friday slot is still on.
2) Laura/Rishi — can you owners for the evidence pack and capacity reservation? I sketched owners below.

Owners (proposed):
- Evidence + risk log: laura_bennett
- Dedicated pool provisioning + capacity hold: rishi_malhotra
- Commercial/fallout (credits/SLA): ben_carter

I attached a draft MAP update and an open-items snapshot for procurement to review (halcyon_map_v2.xlsx, open_items_snapshot.pdf). Laura/Rishi — please review and update before EOD Thursday so we can push to Eli ahead of Friday.

Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: 2025-10-03T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close timeline concern — staging slippage

Markus/Rishi — quick internal run-through after reviewing the draft MAP and open items. My notes:

- Evidence pack: I can own the 1-page risk log and the acceptance checklist. Will keep it tight: open item, impact (high/med/low), mitigation, owner, ETA. Target: first draft 10/03 by 3pm PT.
- Dedicated pool: Rishi — we will need an infra reservation for 2x A100-equivalent nodes for the 72-hour initial pass + scaled down during second pass. Can you confirm availability and cost delta? If we can hold buffer capacity that removes a procurement objection.
- Retention/KV isolation: engineering can offer a temporary 30-day retention and tenant-specific KV isolation for the canary. Needs a short security sign-off (I will prepare the attestation text).
- Commercial remediation: Ben — if procurement insists on credits we should propose a one-time evaluation credit tied to observable SLAs in the canary window.

Risks to call out explicitly to Halcyon:
1) If procurement pushes a 30-day review, timeline slips to late Nov (we should quantify).
2) Any changes to data residency or networking will require a longer rework (2–3 weeks).

I'll push the draft evidence pack by 3pm and ping Eli.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Eli Thompson <eli.thompson@halcyonhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@halcyonhealth.com
Date: 2025-10-06T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close timeline concern — staging slippage

Markus / team — appreciate the clear plan and the attachments. Procurement confirmed they received the draft MAP and the open-items snapshot; two immediate asks from them and the security council:

1) A written attestation (1 paragraph) that the temporary 30-day retention and KV isolation will be enforced and auditable for the canary period. They want a named owner for the attestation and a contact for audit requests.
2) A commercial contingency: procurement is pushing for a short-term credit if the canary fails due to platform availability or data concerns. They asked us to route a credit ask through your finance lead — can Ben handle an initial offer?

If you can confirm (1) attestation owner and text and (2) a proposed credit range by EOD Tuesday 10/07, procurement will unblock the Friday decision and we can start on 10/09 as you proposed. Otherwise they will need to run a full review and the earliest re-start pushes out ~3 weeks.

Eli
Eli Thompson
Director, Platform Engineering
Halcyon Health
